items.title: 5 Blue-Chip Dividend Stocks Built to Keep Paying Through Tough Markets
items.summary: A fat yield means nothing if the cash isn't there to fund it. Five blue chips face the same coverage test, and two of them pay out with almost no room to spare. Which dividends hold up when markets turn?

items.title: PepsiCo (PEP) Stock May Be 49% Undervalued Following Margin Concerns
items.summary: PepsiCo has seen a muted share price journey in recent years, and investors are increasingly asking whether the current valuation is still supported by the cash the business can generate. With the stock around US$140.54 at the last close, the key issue is how that price lines up against the strength and timing of its future cash flows. items.title: How Many Shares of Coca-Cola or PepsiCo Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAt today’s prices, collecting $1,000 a month in dividends takes 5,661 shares of Coca-Cola, about $549,100, or 2,028 shares of PepsiCo, about $285,000. PepsiCo looks like the better buy for that income, as long as its turnaround gets its free cash flow growing again.
